evidence_items.publisher: Core Scientific, transcript hosted by StockAnalysis
evidence_items.locator: June 12, 2024 Investor Day, Matt Brown's Bitcoin-to-HPC conversion illustration
evidence_items.explanation: The engineering discussion describes adding generators, chillers, batteries, UPS equipment, and GPU systems. It supports the claim that conversion requires substantial new equipment rather than simply putting existing Bitcoin machines to work on AI.

evidence_items.locator: Business overview and HPC transition discussion; Mining Equipment section
evidence_items.explanation: The filing identifies existing infrastructure as an input to the HPC conversion, contradicting the implication that there is no practical reuse path. Separately, it describes the mining hardware as specialized SHA-256 ASICs, reinforcing the distinction between reusing a facility and reusing its mining chips.

evidence_items.publisher: Core Scientific, transcript hosted by StockAnalysis
evidence_items.locator: September 14, 2026 conference, Russell Cann's discussion of the CoreWeave conversions
evidence_items.explanation: Management later described extensive rebuilding for liquid-cooled capacity, materially qualifying its earlier reuse language. This later account concerns construction extending beyond the target period and therefore is context rather than decisive historical outcome evidence.

unresolved_gaps: The sources do not provide an independently verified share of total infrastructure retained or replaced across representative conversions.
